{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzVfXG5BaNs2CrCR7haB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01DrWDppGTkfPsYHnjqes84i","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261012-111947/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-cc-medium_omp_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","old_string":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n    // For each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n                \n                if (newDist < distIJ) {\n                    dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}","new_string":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized over source nodes i.\n    // The k loop must stay sequential. Within phase k, each row i is written\n    // only by the thread that owns it, and row k is read from a snapshot taken\n    // at the start of the phase, so no thread reads a row another thread writes.\n    // Row k is unchanged during phase k because dist[k][k] == 0.\n    std::vector<unsigned int> rowK(numNodes);\n    unsigned int* const d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const p = path.data();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // Implicit barrier at the end orders this copy after phase k-1 and before phase k\n        #pragma omp single\n        std::copy(d + k * numNodes, d + (k + 1) * numNodes, rowK.data());\n\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            unsigned int* const distI = d + i * numNodes;\n            unsigned int* const pathI = p + i * numNodes;\n            const unsigned int distIK = distI[k];\n\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool improved = newDist < distI[j];\n                distI[j] = improved ? newDist : distI[j];\n                pathI[j] = improved ? static_cast<unsigned int>(k) : pathI[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":649,"cache_read_input_tokens":25615,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":649},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a9a5405-9b16-4f3b-ad1c-d37e26a1e05c","uuid":"64bcc8d3-eb03-4892-8508-d80e966766a3","timestamp":"2026-10-13T15:45:15.487Z","request_id":"req_011CfzVfWk5ABD5WYMMpQoN9"}

Within phase k, each row i is written\n    // only by the thread that owns it, and row k is read from a snapshot taken\n    // at the start of the phase, so no thread reads a row another thread writes.\n    // Row k is unchanged during phase k because dist[k][k] == 0.\n    std::vector<unsigned int> rowK(numNodes);\n    unsigned int* const d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const p = path.data();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // Implicit barrier at the end orders this copy after phase k-1 and before phase k\n        #pragma omp single\n        std::copy(d + k * numNodes, d + (k + 1) * numNodes, rowK.data());\n\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            unsigned int* const distI = d + i * numNodes;\n            unsigned int* const pathI = p + i * numNodes;\n            const unsigned int distIK = distI[k];\n\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool improved = newDist < distI[j];\n                distI[j] = improved ? newDist : distI[j];\n                pathI[j] = improved ? static_cast<unsigned int>(k) : pathI[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a9a5405-9b16-4f3b-ad1c-d37e26a1e05c","uuid":"70dd6681-e981-4e35-8d98-dc44aed9bc2b","timestamp":"2026-10-13T15:52:22.831Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"./common/hash.hpp\n./common/results_output.hpp\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized over source nodes i.\n    // The k loop must stay sequential. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzWDXiVnBqPA4XFKkuf2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall kernel now runs in parallel with OpenMP. The output matches the original, and the scaling is good up to about 8–16 threads.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- **`floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp`**: `floydWarshall` keeps the sequential k loop. Within each phase, rows `i` are split across threads with a static schedule. Row k is copied to a buffer at the start of each phase, so no thread reads a row that another thread is writing. The inner j loop is branchless and marked `#pragma omp simd`.\n- **`floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. There are no `#ifdef` guards, so the build always uses OpenMP. The executable name and compile flags are unchanged.\n\nI didn't create any files in the project. The build was done out-of-tree in `/tmp`, and `output.txt` is untouched.\n\n**Choices I made**\n\n- Left `initializeDistanceMatrix` sequential. Its `rand_r` stream is stateful, and parallelizing it would change the generated matrix.\n- Left `initializePathMatrix`, `validateResult`, and the hash/print code sequential. They are outside the timed region, and changing them had no measurable effect.\n- Did not switch to tiled (blocked) Floyd-Warshall. It would scale better, but it changes the order of updates, which can change `path` on ties. `path` is not printed, but I didn't want to change the semantics without you asking.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- **Equivalence**: a scratch harness in `/tmp` compared `dist` and `path` against the original kernel for sizes 1 to 1000 and three weight ranges. It matched at 1, 2, 4, 16, and 256 threads. The shipped binary's output also matched the original (hash, min/max, samples, validation) for n = 1, 7, 100, 512, 1000.\n- **Race check**: ThreadSanitizer reports data races in the OpenMP build. I believe they are false positives, because libgomp is not instrumented and TSan can't see its barriers. To check this, I wrote the same phase structure with `std::thread` and `std::barrier` in `/tmp`. It ran clean under TSan, and a deliberately broken variant was flagged, so the check does catch races. This is indirect evidence, not a proof about the OpenMP build.\n\n**Timings** (computation time, single runs on 2× AMD EPYC 7763, 256 hardware threads)\n\n| n | original | 1 thread | 8 threads | 16 threads | 32 threads | 64 threads |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | 45 ms | 13 ms | 13 ms | 16 ms | 25 ms |\n| 1024 | 1227 ms | 356 ms | 64 ms | 49 ms | 40 ms | 40 ms |\n| 2048 | 9397 ms | 3008 ms | 401 ms | 413 ms | 541 ms | 308 ms |\n\nSingle-thread speedup comes from the vectorized inner loop. Beyond about 8–16 threads the gain flattens, mostly because each phase streams the whole matrix from memory. The n=2048 numbers are noisy, which is expected from single runs.\n\nI did not commit anything, since you didn't ask for a commit."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":502,"cache_read_input_tokens":47536,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":502},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a9a5405-9b16-4f3b-ad1c-d37e26a1e05c","uuid":"d1d8e23a-86f5-49ec-b7d5-4fbe43983ef6","timestamp":"2026-10-13T15:52:31.627Z","request_id":"req_011CfzWDXNQpEtedWSef4iAt"}

There are no `#ifdef` guards, so the build always uses OpenMP. The executable name and compile flags are unchanged.\n\nI didn't create any files in the project. The build was done out-of-tree in `/tmp`, and `output.txt` is untouched.\n\n**Choices I made**\n\n- Left `initializeDistanceMatrix` sequential. Its `rand_r` stream is stateful, and parallelizing it would change the generated matrix.\n- Left `initializePathMatrix`, `validateResult`, and the hash/print code sequential. They are outside the timed region, and changing them had no measurable effect.\n- Did not switch to tiled (blocked) Floyd-Warshall. It would scale better, but it changes the order of updates, which can change `path` on ties. `path` is not printed, but I didn't want to change the semantics without you asking.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- **Equivalence**: a scratch harness in `/tmp` compared `dist` and `path` against the original kernel for sizes 1 to 1000 and three weight ranges. It matched at 1, 2, 4, 16, and 256 threads. The shipped binary's output also matched the original (hash, min/max, samples, validation) for n = 1, 7, 100, 512, 1000.\n- **Race check**: ThreadSanitizer reports data races in the OpenMP build. I believe they are false positives, because libgomp is not instrumented and TSan can't see its barriers. To check this, I wrote the same phase structure with `std::thread` and `std::barrier` in `/tmp`. It ran clean under TSan, and a deliberately broken variant was flagged, so the check does catch races. This is indirect evidence, not a proof about the OpenMP build.\n\n**Timings** (computation time, single runs on 2× AMD EPYC 7763, 256 hardware threads)\n\n| n | original | 1 thread | 8 threads | 16 threads | 32 threads | 64 threads |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | 45 ms | 13 ms | 13 ms | 16 ms | 25 ms |\n| 1024 | 1227 ms | 356 ms | 64 ms | 49 ms | 40 ms | 40 ms |\n| 2048 | 9397 ms | 3008 ms | 401 ms | 413 ms | 541 ms | 308 ms |\n\nSingle-thread speedup comes from the vectorized inner loop. Beyond about 8–16 threads the gain flattens, mostly because each phase streams the whole matrix from memory.
